what: The brief asked for a planted bug 'a parent repaired before its child' that ends stale. In the model as it was (Leaf, Mid, Top) no order of repair can be stale: every parent that reads the world also reads only entries the same change queues, and a queued entry is dropped at once, so the parent's lookup repairs it on demand. The hole needs a parent with a reader of its own that reads the world and a value two steps above a fact; the model had no such step, so the control could not have been written and the scope would have 'proved' an order it never exercised.
cost: an hour of design before any code; one new step (`Over`) and one new way in the exhaustive model
whys: why no order was stale: the model's only parent that reads the world (Mid) reads leaves directly, and the top has no reader, so it is dropped, not repaired
why the model had that shape: it was built for nesting and early cutoff, where two levels under a top are enough
why that matters: an exhaustive check proves only what its model can reach, and nothing said which invariants the model can violate
cause: a model's reach was implicit: each invariant's shortest violating shape was not written down beside the model
class: an exhaustive check whose scope cannot express the bug a new invariant guards against, so its control is vacuous or impossible
prevention: each invariant gets its control before the invariant is claimed, and the model's doc says the shape each control needs (nested.rs's header does, for `Over` and the warm start)
fix: done: `Over` (reads a fact and a Mid; `Over(1)` reads `Over(0)`) and `Start::Warm` (a store another session filled, for a hit admitted then carried, which four steps from an empty store cannot reach)
